course.name: COMP4348 COMP5348 Enterprise Scale Software Architecture

rubric.long_description: Classifies the state the system keeps as resource, session, local computation or derived, or another appropriate category if justified, with plausible examples for each and a rationale distinguishing them.

ratings.long_description: All four categories identified, or an appropriate alternative categorisation justified, with plausible examples and a rationale; derived values (overdue flags, counts, roll-up status) not treated as authoritative resource state.
Two or three categories handled correctly, or examples given but mis-categorised in places.
Only resource state discussed, or categories named with no meaningful examples.

rubric.long_description: Main persistent entities (project; task with self-referencing parent for sub-tasks; user; team; team membership; task assignment), their key attributes and relationships.

ratings.long_description: Entity set supports nesting and team/developer assignment; key attributes and relationships stated; assignment not duplicated across Task, User and Team without a stated consistency mechanism.
Main entities present but the sub-task self-reference or the assignment relationship is missing, vague, or redundantly duplicated without justification.
No usable data model, or the model cannot represent nested tasks or assignment.

rubric.description: Q1(c) Developer task view, derived state and constraints
rubric.long_description: Retrieval of a developer's own tasks; overdue = due_date < today AND status not in {resolved, done}; due soon = today <= due_date <= today + 7 days. At least one item of derived state and two integrity constraints.

ratings.long_description: Retrieval path stated (developer id from session, query on assignment), both date predicates correct including the status exclusion, one derived item and two valid constraints given.
Retrieval or predicates broadly right but the status exclusion is missing, the seven-day boundary is wrong, or fewer than two valid constraints are given.
No workable retrieval mechanism, or overdue and due-soon logic absent or incorrect.

rubric.long_description: Trade-off between recomputing aggregates on demand and materialising them; one consistency risk created by materialisation; one mechanism for keeping materialised values correct.

ratings.long_description: Trade-off argued in both directions; a specific risk named (stale ancestor roll-ups / write amplification, or time-dependent flags going stale with no write at all); a workable maintenance mechanism described.
A position is taken and one side of the trade-off argued, but the consistency risk is generic or no maintenance mechanism is given.
No trade-off discussion, or materialisation recommended with no acknowledgement of any consistency obligation.

rubric.long_description: Memory is the binding constraint: 8/4 = 2 Type A per D2 v3, so 24 instances; floor(64/12) = 5 Type B per D16 v3, so 15 instances.

ratings.long_description: Both packing factors and both instance counts correct, with memory shown as the binding constraint.
One of the two packings or counts correct, or the right method with an arithmetic slip (e.g. not flooring 64/12).
Neither packing correct, or capacity derived from something other than memory without justification.

rubric.description: Q2(1b) Runtimes, cost and elapsed time
rubric.long_description: Runtime = max(CPU, I/O) with capacity shared equally: Type A 1,200 s, Type B 84.375 s. Cost_A $1.5040, Cost_B $0.52875, total about $2.033. Elapsed time 1,200 s. Wrong steps deduct 0.5; correct final values worth 0.5.

ratings.long_description: Both runtimes correct via max(CPU, I/O) with equal sharing, both costs pro-rated to exact runtime, total and elapsed time correct.
Correct method (max of CPU and I/O, equal sharing, pro-rated billing) but one runtime, cost, total or the elapsed time wrong.
Runtimes not derived from max(CPU, I/O), sharing ignored, or hourly rates applied without pro-rating.

rubric.long_description: Answers no, and justifies it from the constant per-vCPU ratios in the table: 4 GB RAM, 100 IOPS, $0.094 per vCPU-hour and 2x10^9 instructions per second for every instance size.

ratings.long_description: States no and derives it from the per-vCPU ratios, showing that a fully packed instance gives each task the same share regardless of instance size.
Correct conclusion but the justification is asserted rather than derived from the resource and price ratios.
Wrong conclusion, or a bare no with no reference to the ratios in the table.

rubric.description: Q2(2b) Both task types and a changed assumption
rubric.long_description: Addresses Type A and Type B separately, including that D2 v3 is infeasible for Type B on memory, and changes one assumption the conclusion depends on, with brief reasoning. Any such assumption is acceptable, including those stated in the question body; it need not be one of the two bulleted assumptions.

ratings.long_description: Both task types addressed with the D2 v3 memory infeasibility noted, and one change to any assumption the conclusion depends on, with a brief explanation of why it would make a different instance size cheaper (for example a fixed per-instance startup charge, volume discounts, non-proportional pricing, heterogeneous processors, contention, or imperfect scaling).
Only one task type addressed, or a change named without explaining why it would make a different instance size cheaper.
Neither task type justified, and no changed assumption identified.

rubric.description: Q3(a) Interleaving and why one writer suffices
rubric.long_description: A concrete interleaving in the issue-tracking setting: initial values, numbered interleaved steps, and the incorrect result the read-only activity observes. Explains that interference needs only shared data and one writer.

ratings.long_description: Initial values stated, steps interleaved so the reader straddles the writer's update, the wrong result shown, and the one-writer point made explicitly.
An interleaving is given but initial values or the incorrect observed result are missing, the steps are not genuinely interleaved, or the one-writer conclusion is not drawn.
No interleaving, or a scenario requiring two writers, which does not answer the question.

rubric.description: Q3(b) Anomaly named and prevention mechanism
rubric.long_description: Names the anomaly (inconsistent read / inconsistent analysis) and states one concurrency-control mechanism with a brief explanation of how it prevents it.

ratings.long_description: Anomaly correctly named and a valid mechanism (serializable isolation, snapshot isolation, or two-phase locking with shared locks held to end of transaction) explained in terms of this interleaving.
Anomaly named but the mechanism only named without explanation, or a valid mechanism explained under a wrong or vague anomaly name.
Anomaly not identified or misidentified (e.g. as lost update or deadlock), and no valid mechanism given.
